title: Drink finder
evidenceStatus: 24 authored fully specified requests; 23 completed correctly, 1 HTTP 429; 2 unscored ambiguity examples; live contract differs from recorded runner
summary: The completed examples cover eight supported attribute profiles and a four-substring baseline matches Jev on all 23. The live component uses a different response contract, does not enforce extracted requirements, and offers no actual clarification conversation. Build Cafe Jev around semantic preference extraction, deterministic recipe constraints, visible customization and seeded customer goals.
strengths: Fixed fictional menu is passed to Jev and shown to visitors.
Live drink options include an explicit none answer.
Published data distinguish 23 correct completed calls from one provider overload.
The adjacent Adaptive forms experiment already provides exact matching and all 81 partial preference states.
Live requests use the visitor key from memory.

findings.title: The evaluation only tests supported complete profiles
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/compositions.py:258 and :329; probes/beverage.py: 23/23 literal-phrase baseline matches, 22 unique completed strings, 8 of 16 complete attribute profiles unsupported but unscored
findings.impact: The reported perfect completed accuracy says little about ambiguity, impossible constraints, customization or discovering preferences.
findings.fix: Keep the current set as a smoke test; evaluate all 81 partial states, independent language realizations, no-match cases and multi-turn goals.

findings.title: The recorded and live contracts disagree
findings.evidence: src/jev_lab/compositions.py:294 has 8 drink options and 5 questions; experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:541 has 9 drink options and 2 questions; clarify changes from numeric to categorical
findings.impact: The published run does not validate the actual live workflow, and the initial answer belongs to a different request from the text area.
findings.fix: Use one versioned schema and store exact request text, menu/prompt revision and request ID; record that same contract.

findings.title: The component never checks constraints independently
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:559 directly applies the model drink; :564 can simultaneously show an unresolved clarification; no preference extraction or feasible-set validator in Beverage
findings.impact: An impossible or premature suggestion can appear as a valid result; none renders as a cup titled None.
findings.fix: Extract typed required/preferred/unknown/conflicting preferences, validate recipes in code, rank only feasible candidates, and render separate clarification/conflict/no-match states.

findings.title: Results can become stale or misleading after editing
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:512 changes only selected; :530 changes only input; :559 accepts all completions; shared.tsx:214 has no request revision guard
findings.impact: A displayed suggestion or inspected answer can refer to an older request or a different manual choice.
findings.fix: Separate draft and submitted state, label manual actions, cancel obsolete work and ignore responses from older request/session revisions.

findings.title: The cafe does not support a recipe or conversation
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/agent-experiments.tsx:494 always renders steam; :515 omits sweetness; :567 clarification has no answer control; menu is duplicated at :473, journeys.tsx:6 and compositions.py:246
findings.impact: The visitor cannot discover a preference or customize a drink, and the visual barely reflects the model decision.
findings.fix: Use one recipe catalog with legal modifiers, prices and availability; add conversation controls, illustrated cup changes and a visible receipt.

simulation.title: Cafe Jev: from an uncertain craving to a custom drink
simulation.description: A seeded customer arrives, browses an illustrated menu, states a craving, answers one useful question at a time, revises preferences, customizes legal ingredients and confirms a simulated receipt. A private customer goal independently scores the final recipe; complete turns and decisions are replayable.
simulation.jevsRole: Interpret language as typed hard/soft preferences, rank feasible recipes, and choose the next question or supported action without access to the hidden goal.
simulation.codeRole: Own menu/ingredient facts, prices, inventory, allowed modifiers, feasible recipes, request revisions, state transitions, visuals and independent terminal scoring.
acceptanceCriteria: Arrival, clarification, customization, revision, undo and receipt replay work in one session.
Identical seeds and actions reproduce customer answers, inventory and outcomes.
Invalid ingredients, inventory and explicit budgets never pass confirmation; semantic extraction errors remain separately measurable.
Cup appearance reflects temperature, size and ingredients, with reduced-motion alternatives.
Recorded replay works without a key and live mode uses the visitor key; manual, recorded and live choices remain distinct.
Obsolete responses cannot alter a newer draft or session.
Full customer text, menu facts and model decisions remain inspectable.

evaluation.design: Enumerate all 81 partial states and 16 complete profiles. Create 4 independent language realizations per partial state and run 3 option-order seeds, 972 logical requests. Use 24 separate development situations and a locked 120-scenario multi-turn test, 3 option-order seeds, at most 6 turns, at most 2160 additional requests. Total main test at most 3132 calls per policy plus retries. Use independently annotated goals and deterministic scripted responses; evaluate raw decisions separately from guarded execution. Report scenario-cluster bootstrap intervals and per-condition counts. Proposed release targets: zero confirmed hard-constraint violations in the 120 scenarios, at least 95% feasible-goal completion within six turns, fewer questions than the fixed questionnaire without worse task success. Later run 24-person counterbalanced usability study with 3 tasks each.
baselines: Literal phrase parser plus exact menu filter
Information-gain question policy with oracle structured preferences
Uniform and simple weighted ranking among identical feasible recipes
metrics: Preference extraction exact match and per-field accuracy
Hard-constraint violations before and after guards
Utility regret over independently accepted recipes
Clarifications per successful order and redundant questions
Completed-call latency, end-to-end latency, retries and provider availability

coverage.current: 24 requests repeating 8 complete supported profiles; 23 completed, 1 provider overload; 2 unscored ambiguous cases; 22 unique completed strings.
coverage.full: No external official split. Current finite domain is 81 partial preference states: 16 no-match, 29 unique-match, 36 multi-match; 16 complete profiles, of which 8 have no supported drink.
coverage.feasibility: Full finite state coverage is trivial in code. Proposed language plus multi-turn test is at most 3132 logical model calls per policy; exact text and accepted goals must be authored/reviewed first.

libraries.name: XState
libraries.use: Optional customer-session machines, invoked asynchronous Jev requests and replayable snapshots; a reducer is sufficient for an initial single-customer version.

libraries.name: Motion
libraries.use: Already installed; animate changes to menu candidates, cup ingredients and counter/receipt layout so decisions have visible consequences.

libraries.name: Zod
libraries.use: Already installed; validate recipe variants, modifiers, ranges and shared response contracts; semantic extraction still needs independent evaluation.
